newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Burkina Faso to issue first ever bond - Belgolaise.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso to issue first ever bond - Belgolaise.

text.p: West African state Burkina Faso plans to issue its first ever bond on December 11, Belgian bank Belgolaise SA said in a bulletin.

The five-year, five billion Central African Franc (CFA) bond will be issued in the form of one million certificates with a face value of 5,000 CFA. The issue price and coupon have not yet been fixed, Belgolaise, which owns 25 percent of Banque Internationale du Burkina, said.
"Investors can subscribe from anywhere on the national territory as well as in Burkina Faso embassies in countries where Burkinabe people are numerous," Belgolaise said.
Belgolaise said the bond was to fund development in rural areas where access to traditional forms of bank credit was difficult. The funds would be distributed locally via cooperative banks.
The government in Ouagadougou is aiming for gross domestic product (GDP) growth in excess of five percent and a 10 percent reduction in external debt by 1998, Belgolaise added.
Belgolaise is controlled by Belgium's largest bank, Generale de Banque SA.
